## Functions

Function names are case-insensitive. `name?` is an optional argument, and `…` means that you can give more arguments of the same kind.

### Type conversion

- `date(value: expression) → datetime`
  Converts a datetime or an ISO 8601 datetime string to a date. Time part is truncated.
  Example: `date("2025-03-20")`
- `datetime(value: expression, mode?: string) → datetime`
  Converts a datetime string or bytes to a datetime.
  `mode`: The mode indicating the format. One of: `"simple"`, `"iso"`, `"simpleBytes"`, `"isoBytes"`, `"unixSeconds"`, `"unixMilliseconds"`, `"unixMicroseconds"`, `"unixNanoseconds"`. Default is `"iso"`.
  Example: `datetime("2025-03-20 12:45:04")`
- `float(value: expression) → number`
  Converts a string to a floating-point number.
  Example: `float([Text Rating])`
- `integer(value: expression) → number`
  The string or float column to convert to integers. Float values are rounded.
  Example: `integer([User ID])`
- `text(value: expression) → string`
  Converts a number or date to text. Useful for applying text filters or joining with other columns based on text comparisons.
  Example: `text([User ID])`
- `today() → datetime`
  Returns the current date.
  Example: `today()`

### Text

- `collate(value: string, collation: string) → string`
  Applies a collation to a text value for sorting and comparison purposes.
  Example: `collate([Name], "en-ci-ai")`
- `concat(value1: expression, value2: expression, …?: string) → string`
  Combine two or more strings of text together.
  Example: `concat([Last Name], ", ", [First Name])`
- `contains(string1: string, string2: string, …?: string, caseSensitivity?: string) → boolean`
  Returns `true` if `$string1` contains `$string2` within it (or `$string3`, etc. if specified).
  `caseSensitivity`: Optional. Set to `"case-insensitive"` to perform a case-insensitive match.
  Example: `contains([Title], "Small", "Medium", "case-insensitive")`
- `doesNotContain(string1: string, string2: string, …?: string, caseSensitivity?: string) → boolean`
  Returns `true` if `$string1` does not contain `$string2` within it (and `$string3`, etc. if specified).
  `caseSensitivity`: Optional. Set to `"case-insensitive"` to perform a case-insensitive match.
  Example: `doesNotContain([Title], "Small", "Medium", "case-insensitive")`
- `domain(urlOrEmail: string) → string`
  Extracts the domain name (eg. `"metabase"`) from a URL or email
  Example: `domain([Email])`
- `endsWith(string1: string, string2: string, …?: string, caseSensitivity?: string) → boolean`
  Returns true if the end of the `$string1` matches the `$string2` (or `$string3`, etc. if specified).
  `caseSensitivity`: Optional. Set to `"case-insensitive"` to perform a case-insensitive match.
  Example: `endsWith([Title], "Small", "Medium", "case-insensitive")`
- `host(urlOrEmail: string) → string`
  Extracts the host (domain name and TLD, eg. `"metabase.com"` from `"status.metabase.com"`) from a URL or email
  Example: `host([Email])`
- `isEmpty(column: expression) → boolean`
  Checks if a column is empty
  Example: `isEmpty([Name])`
- `length(value: string) → number`
  Returns the number of characters in text.
  Example: `length([Comment])`
- `lower(value: string) → string`
  Returns the string of text in all lower case.
  Example: `lower([Status])`
- `lTrim(value: string) → string`
  Removes leading whitespace from a string of text.
  Example: `lTrim([Comment])`
- `notEmpty(column: expression) → boolean`
  Checks if a column is not empty
  Example: `notEmpty([Name])`
- `path(url: string) → string`
  Extracts the pathname from a URL. E.g., `path("https://www.example.com/path/to/page.html?key1=value)` would return `/path/to/page.html`.
  Example: `path([URL])`
- `regexExtract(value: string, regular_expression: string) → string`
  Extracts matching substrings according to a regular expression.
  Example: `regexExtract([Address], "[0-9]+")`
- `replace(value: string, find: string, replace: string) → string`
  Replaces a part of the input text with new text.
  Example: `replace([Title], "Enormous", "Gigantic")`
- `rTrim(value: string) → string`
  Removes trailing whitespace from a string of text.
  Example: `rTrim([Comment])`
- `splitPart(text: string, delimiter: string, position: number) → string`
  Splits a string on a specified delimiter and returns the nth substring.
  Example: `splitPart([Title], ",", 1)`
- `startsWith(string1: string, string2: string, …?: string, caseSensitivity?: string) → boolean`
  Returns true if the beginning of the `$string1` matches the `$string2` (or `$string3`, etc. if specified).
  `caseSensitivity`: Optional. Set to `"case-insensitive"` to perform a case-insensitive match.
  Example: `startsWith([Title], "Small", "Medium", "case-insensitive")`
- `subdomain(url: string) → string`
  Extracts the first subdomain (eg. `"status"` from `"status.metabase.com"`, `""` from `"bbc.co.uk"`) from a URL. Ignores `"www"`.
  Example: `subdomain([ProfileImage])`
- `substring(value: string, position: number, length: number) → string`
  Returns a portion of the supplied text.
  Example: `substring([Title], 1, 10)`
- `trim(value: string) → string`
  Removes leading and trailing whitespace from a string of text.
  Example: `trim([Comment])`
- `upper(value: string) → string`
  Returns the text in all upper case.
  Example: `upper([Status])`

### Date and time

- `convertTimezone(column: datetime, target: string, source?: string) → datetime`
  Convert timezone of a date or timestamp column. We support tz database time zone names.
  Example: `convertTimezone([Created At], "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh", "UTC")`
- `datetimeAdd(column: datetime, amount: number, unit: string) → datetime`
  Adds some units of time to a date or timestamp value.
  `unit`: Choose from: year, quarter, month, week, day, hour, minute, second, or millisecond.
  Example: `datetimeAdd([Created At], 1, "month")`
- `datetimeDiff(datetime1: datetime, datetime2: datetime, unit: string) → number`
  Get the difference between two datetime values (`$datetime2` minus `$datetime1`) using the specified unit of time.
  `unit`: Choose from: year, quarter, month, week, day, hour, minute, or second.
  Example: `datetimeDiff([Created At], [Shipped At], "month")`
- `datetimeSubtract(column: datetime, amount: number, unit: string) → datetime`
  Subtracts some units of time to a date or timestamp value.
  `unit`: Choose from: year, quarter, month, week, day, hour, minute, second, or millisecond.
  Example: `datetimeSubtract([Created At], 1, "month")`
- `day(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer (`1`-`31`) with the number of the day of the month.
  Example: `day([Created At])`
- `dayName(dayNumber: number) → string`
  Returns the localized name of a day of the week, given the day's number.
  Example: `dayName([Weekday])`
- `hour(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer (`0`-`23`) with the number of the hour. No AM/PM.
  Example: `hour([Created At])`
- `interval(column: expression, number: number, unit: string) → boolean`
  Checks a date column's values to see if they're within the relative range.
  Example: `interval([Created At], -1, "month")`
- `intervalStartingFrom(column: expression, value: number, unit: string, offsetValue: number, offsetUnit: string) → boolean`
  Returns true if a column's value falls within an interval, starting from an initial, offsetting interval.
  Example: `intervalStartingFrom([Created At], -20, "month", -10, "year")`
- `minute(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer (`0`-`59`) with the number of the minute in the hour.
  Example: `minute([Created At])`
- `month(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer (`1`-`12`) with the number of the month in the year.
  Example: `month([Created At])`
- `monthName(monthNumber: number) → string`
  Returns the localized short name (eg. `"Apr"`) for the given month number (eg. `4`)
  Example: `monthName([Birthday Month])`
- `now() → datetime`
  Returns the current timestamp (in milliseconds).
  Example: `now()`
- `quarter(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer (`1`-`4`) with the number of the quarter in the year.
  Example: `quarter([Created At])`
- `quarterName(quarterNumber: number) → string`
  Returns a string like `"Q1"`, given the quarter number
  Example: `quarterName([Fiscal Quarter])`
- `relativeDateTime(number: number, unit: string) → expression`
  Gets a timestamp relative to the current time
  Example: `relativeDateTime(-30, "day")`
- `second(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer (`0`-`59`) with the number of the seconds in the minute.
  Example: `second([Created At])`
- `timeSpan(number: number, unit: string) → number`
  Gets a time interval of specified length
  Example: `timeSpan(7, "day")`
- `week(column: datetime, mode?: string) → number`
  Extracts the week of the year as an integer.
  `mode`: Optional. The default is `"ISO"`. - ISO: Week 1 starts on the Monday before the first Thursday of January. - US: Week 1 starts on Jan 1. All other weeks start on Sunday. - Instance: Week 1 starts on Jan 1. All other weeks start on the day defined in your Metabase localization settings.
  Example: `week([Created At], "iso")`
- `weekday(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer (`1`-`7`) with the number of the day of the week. Which day is `1` is defined in your localization settings.
  Example: `weekday([Created At])`
- `year(column: datetime) → number`
  Takes a datetime and returns an integer with the number of the year.
  Example: `year([Created At])`

### Math

- `abs(column: number) → number`
  Returns the absolute (positive) value of the specified column.
  Example: `abs([Debt])`
- `ceil(column: number) → number`
  Rounds a decimal number up.
  Example: `ceil([Price])`
- `exp(column: number) → number`
  Returns Euler's number, e, raised to the power of the supplied number.
  Example: `exp([Interest Months])`
- `floor(column: number) → number`
  Rounds a decimal number down.
  Example: `floor([Price])`
- `log(column: number) → number`
  Returns the base 10 log of the number.
  Example: `log([Value])`
- `power(column: number, exponent: number) → number`
  Raises a number to the power of the exponent value.
  Example: `power([Length], 2)`
- `round(column: number) → number`
  Rounds a decimal number either up or down to the nearest integer value.
  Example: `round([Temperature])`
- `sqrt(column: number) → number`
  Returns the square root.
  Example: `sqrt([Hypotenuse])`

### Logic and conditions

- `between(column: expression, start: expression, end: expression) → boolean`
  Checks a date or number column's values to see if they're within the specified range.
  Example: `between([Created At], "2019-01-01", "2022-12-31")`
- `case(condition: expression, output: expression, …?: expression) → expression`
  Alias for `if()`. Tests an expression against a list of cases and returns the corresponding value of the first matching case, with an optional default value if nothing else is met.
  Example: `case([Weight] > 200, "Large", [Weight] > 150, "Medium", "Small")`
- `coalesce(value1: expression, value2: expression, …?: expression) → expression`
  Looks at the values in each argument in order and returns the first non-null value for each row.
  Example: `coalesce([Comments], [Notes], "No comments")`
- `if(condition: expression, output: expression, …?: expression) → expression`
  Alias for `case()`. Tests an expression against a list of cases and returns the corresponding value of the first matching case, with an optional default value if nothing else is met.
  Example: `if([Weight] > 200, "Large", [Weight] > 150, "Medium", "Small")`
- `in(value1: expression, value2: expression, …?: expression) → boolean`
  Returns true if `value1` equals `$value2` (or `$value3`, etc. if specified).
  Example: `in([Category], "Widget", "Gadget")`
- `isNull(column: expression) → boolean`
  Checks if a column is null
  Example: `isNull([Discount])`
- `notIn(value1: expression, value2: expression, …?: expression) → boolean`
  Returns true if `$value1` doesn't equal `$value2` (and `$value3`, etc. if specified).
  Example: `notIn([Category], "Widget", "Gadget")`
- `notNull(column: expression) → boolean`
  Checks if a column is not null
  Example: `notNull([Discount])`

### Aggregations (only in aggregation mode)

- `Average(column: number) → aggregation`
  Returns the average of the values in the column.
  Example: `Average([Quantity])`
- `Count() → aggregation`
  Returns the count of rows in the selected data.
  Example: `Count()`
- `CountIf(condition: boolean) → aggregation`
  Only counts rows where the condition is `true`.
  Example: `CountIf([Subtotal] > 100)`
- `Distinct(column: expression) → aggregation`
  The number of distinct values in this column.
  Example: `Distinct([Last Name])`
- `DistinctIf(column: number, condition: boolean) → aggregation`
  The count of distinct values in this column for rows where the condition is `true`.
  Example: `DistinctIf([Customer ID], [Order Status] = "Completed")`
- `Max(column: expression) → aggregation`
  Returns the largest value found in the column.
  Example: `Max([Age])`
- `Median(column: number) → aggregation`
  Returns the median of all the values of a column.
  Example: `Median([Quantity])`
- `Min(column: expression) → aggregation`
  Returns the smallest value found in the column
  Example: `Min([Salary])`
- `Percentile(column: number, percentile-value: number) → aggregation`
  Returns the value of the column at the percentile value.
  Example: `Percentile([Score], 0.9)`
- `Share(condition: boolean) → aggregation`
  Returns the percent of rows in the data that match the condition, as a decimal.
  Example: `Share([Source] = "Google")`
- `StandardDeviation(column: number) → aggregation`
  Calculates the standard deviation of the column.
  Example: `StandardDeviation([Population])`
- `Sum(column: number) → aggregation`
  Adds up all the values of the column.
  Example: `Sum([Subtotal])`
- `SumIf(column: number, condition: boolean) → aggregation`
  Sums up the specified column only for rows where the condition is `true`.
  Example: `SumIf([Subtotal], [Order Status] = "Valid")`
- `Variance(column: number) → aggregation`
  Returns the numeric variance for a given column.
  Example: `Variance([Temperature])`

### Window functions (only in aggregation mode)

- `CumulativeCount() → aggregation`
  The additive total of rows across a breakout.
  Example: `CumulativeCount()`
- `CumulativeSum(column: number) → aggregation`
  The rolling sum of a column across a breakout.
  Example: `CumulativeSum([Subtotal])`
- `Offset(expression: any, rowOffset: number) → any`
  Returns the value of an aggregation expression in a different row
  Example: `Offset(Sum([Total]), -1)`
